heading: What each realm refuses
body:
Every annotation above appears in each language that accepts it. The missing examples are not mistakes. The compiler rejects these combinations before anything runs, and its error message says why.

A native Tac service is a Swift, Kotlin, C# or Rust service that Tachyon links into a native companion. It carries the Service marker like every class in client/services (TY1363). It accepts Service, Lifetime, NeedsAll, Needs, Named, the data and behavior annotations, Setup, CacheSettings, Entity, Table, Store, Checked, Settings, WhenProfile, WhenSetting and HTTPClient. A native companion has no page storage and no page transport, so its Setup names every cache and entity adapter that the service uses, and the native build stops when one is missing (ADR 0059). Its HTTPClient sends requests through the HTTP adapter that its Setup names. A native Rust service injects a Helper with Needs, a Swift service builds the Helper that its Needs field names, a native C# service builds one with `new`, and a Kotlin service or Helper names one in a Needs field, which makes a new Helper for it. A linked native service cannot use page-only APIs such as PreferenceStrings and DocumentTitle. It receives the native WindowControls and FilePicker providers instead (ADR 0089; see Native services). StreamRequest and SocketRequest clients are written in every Tac service language: JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Ruby, Rust, Dart, Swift, Kotlin, Java, C#, Lua, Python, F# and C++. The page's JavaScript holds the connection for a Go, Ruby, Rust, Dart, Java, Lua, Python or C++ service, for a Swift, Kotlin or C# web service and for an F# service in the browser. A native Kotlin build and a natively linked C# or F# service refuse them, because no page holds the connection there.

Lua, Python and C++ are Tac service languages with limits. This table lists what each one refuses.

| Language | What the build refuses in Tac code |
| --- | --- |
| Lua (ADR 0085) | TY1308 for the behavior annotations (Setup, Settings, Setting, WhenProfile, WhenSetting, CacheSettings, Cached, ClearCache, UpdateCache, Retry, MaxAtOnce, AllOrNothing, Checked, Check and the field checks), Entity, Store, Query, HTTPClient and its request annotations, LocalState, SessionState, Helper, Fake, TestSettings and FreshStart. Lua has no WindowControls. TY2015 for a Needs field whose type is another service. It accepts Service, Lifetime, Needs, Named, NeedsAll, OnStart, OnStop, OnEvent, Order, InBackground, Topic, Converter, Convert, Test, TestSetup, UseProfiles and ValueSource. |
| Python (ADR 0093) | TY1605 for an `async def` OnStop or OnEvent and the browser API resources. A Python Check cannot read a Checked model from client/models yet (TY1308), and a Python Needs field cannot name a Converter yet (TY1605). Python accepts Service, Lifetime, Needs, Named, NeedsAll, Helper, `async def` methods, OnStart (plain or `async def`), plain OnStop and OnEvent with their options, ApplicationEventPublisher, Topic, LocalState, SessionState, the caching annotations, PageDefaults, Retry, MaxAtOnce, AllOrNothing, Store, Query, HTTPClient with its request annotations, StreamRequest and SocketRequest, Test, TestSetup, UseProfiles and ValueSource. |
| C++ (ADR 0099) | TY1308 for a behavior annotation such as Cached or Retry on a `Task` method or an HTTPClient method. TY1372 for a Store adapter other than `"indexeddb"`, for Lifetime `"application"`, and for a `Needs` field that names a browser API. TY1371 for a file that is not one header-only class, for a lowercase marker such as `[[service]]`, and for Setup outside client/setups. C++ accepts every other Tac annotation, including Setup with WhenProfile and WhenSetting, Settings, Entity, Store, Query, the behavior annotations on synchronous service methods, HTTPClient with its request annotations, StreamRequest and SocketRequest, and Test, TestSetup, UseProfiles, TestSettings, Fake, FreshStart and ValueSource. |

Other languages refuse fewer annotations. A Kotlin or Java Helper is a new object for each class that names it in a Needs field, so it takes no NeedsAll, Lifetime, OnStart, OnStop or OnEvent. The build stops such a Helper at the Helper file. A Go Helper belongs to the service that needs or creates it, so it has no Needs, NeedsAll, Lifetime or lifecycle hooks of its own; the build stops those with TY1308 or TY1405. A Java service can ask for another Java service with Needs: the field gets the service of its exact class, and Named picks another provider class, such as a subclass service; the build refuses, with TY1406, a needed service that is Lifetime prototype or NeedsAll, a field that cannot tell which service it means, services that need each other in a circle, and a Named that names no Java service of the page (see A service that needs another service: Tac). An F# Needs property takes the ApplicationEventPublisher, an HTTPClient or another F# service of the page, so the build stops a Needs property of a C# service or of a browser API such as Clock with TY1405, and a needed F# service that has one instance for each component, or a circle of needs, with TY1406. An F# service builds a browser API itself, as in `let clock = Clock()`. A Ruby service cannot ask for another service with Needs either; the build stops it with TY2015 (ADR 0054).

The build also checks where each annotation is written (ADR 0056). It refuses an annotation on the wrong kind of member, such as Cached on a field. It refuses arguments on an annotation that takes none, such as Service, and a missing argument list on one that needs it, such as Test or Named. It refuses an annotation that needs an instance method, such as a route, a listener or Cached, on a static method, the same annotation twice on one member, and two annotations that clash, such as LocalState with SessionState, or Cached with ClearCache. It refuses an annotation without its partner: Order or InBackground without OnEvent, Named without Needs, Id outside an Entity class, and Fake or ValueSource outside a Test or TestSetup class. NeedsAll takes no field list, and a NeedsAll class declares no constructor. Each message names the annotation in your language's spelling, the member, the right place and what the annotation means. These refusals use TY1308.

Every Yon language accepts InBackground listeners (methods that run when an event happens). JavaScript, TypeScript, Python and Dart can make the method asynchronous. Kotlin, C#, F#, Lua, Ruby, Go, Java, Groovy, PHP and Rust keep it synchronous and run it after every other listener of the event. Tac accepts InBackground in every service language that has listeners, because it only delays delivery on the page.

A StreamRoute method (ADR 0058; the old `@Stream` name is retired) returns its values one at a time, so the language needs a way to do that. JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, Kotlin, C#, F#, Dart and Ruby use their own generator syntax, Lua sends each value with `coroutine.yield`, and Go returns an `iter.Seq` (Go's range-over-function iterator). Java and Groovy return a `java.util.stream.Stream` or a `java.util.Iterator`, which gives the values one at a time. Rust returns an `impl Iterator`, which also gives the values one at a time. C++ returns a `tachyon::Generator`, a coroutine that sends each value with `co_yield`.

Both realms refuse a field that Tachyon fills, a Needs field or a NeedsAll field without a starting value, when it is declared nullable. Tachyon never leaves such a field null, so `label?: string` or `final String? path;` would only mislead the reader. The build stops with TY1331 and shows the non-null form to write instead. Both realms also refuse, with TY1332, a field that holds an injected class and does not use the language's variable case, such as `CartStore CartStore;` in Java or `cartStore` in Python.

Gateway exists only in Yon. A Tac service has no supervisor that could start another language for one call. So the annotation fails with TY1308 in every Tac language. Public, SignedIn, Allow and IdentityProvider exist only in Yon, because only a server can decide who may call a route. A Tac page cannot protect data: the server route must say who may call it.
